PIONEER_ERA.name: Pioneer & Front-Engine Era
PIONEER_ERA.aero_type: Streamlined cigar bodies, zero wings, drum & early disc brakes
PIONEER_ERA.key_characteristics: Front-engine transitioning to rear-engine, manual stick-shift, no seatbelts or rollbars, high mechanical mortality.

DFV_WINGS_ERA.name: Cosworth DFV & Wings Revolution
DFV_WINGS_ERA.engine_spec: 3.0L Naturally Aspirated V8 (Ford Cosworth DFV dominance)
DFV_WINGS_ERA.aero_type: Inverted aerofoil wings mounted on suspension uprights, wide slick tyres
DFV_WINGS_ERA.key_characteristics: Introduction of sponsor liveries, downforce aerodynamics, wide tyres, commercial racing explosion.

TURBO_MONSTERS_ERA.name: Ground Effect & 1.5L Turbo Era
TURBO_MONSTERS_ERA.aero_type: Underbody sliding skirts, massive downforce tunnels, active suspension emergence
TURBO_MONSTERS_ERA.key_characteristics: Extreme turbo lag, dangerous qualifying engines lasting 2 laps, carbon-fibre monocoque introduction (McLaren MP4/1).

V10_HIGH_REV_ERA.name: Naturally Aspirated Screaming V10 Era
V10_HIGH_REV_ERA.aero_type: Raised nosecones, bargeboards, complex multi-element diffusers, grooved tyres (1998)
V10_HIGH_REV_ERA.key_characteristics: Mid-race refueling strategies, electronic traction control, instantaneous gear shifts, screaming acoustic engine note.

V8_AERO_KERS_ERA.name: V8 Aerodynamic Refinement & DRS Era
V8_AERO_KERS_ERA.engine_spec: 2.4L Naturally Aspirated V8 (18,000 RPM rev limit)
V8_AERO_KERS_ERA.aero_type: Double diffusers, blown exhaust diffusers, DRS overtaking rear wing (2011)
V8_AERO_KERS_ERA.key_characteristics: Introduction of KERS kinetic electrical boost (2009), Pirelli deliberate tyre degradation cliff, aerodynamic peak.

TURBO_HYBRID_GEN1.name: 1.6L V6 Turbo-Hybrid Era (Gen 1)
TURBO_HYBRID_GEN1.engine_spec: 1.6L Turbo V6 with MGU-K (120 kW) and MGU-H (Unlimited exhaust energy)
TURBO_HYBRID_GEN1.aero_type: Wide track (2017), simplified front wings (2019), titanium Halo cockpit safety device (2018)
TURBO_HYBRID_GEN1.key_characteristics: Over 50% thermal efficiency, massive electrical torque, all-time track lap records set (2020), Mercedes 8-year dominance.

CURRENT_GROUND_EFFECT.name: Modern Ground-Effect & Cost Cap Era (Current Game)
CURRENT_GROUND_EFFECT.engine_spec: 1.6L Turbo V6 Hybrid, E10 10% sustainable ethanol fuel, engine freeze
CURRENT_GROUND_EFFECT.aero_type: Full Venturi underfloor ground-effect tunnels, 18-inch low-profile Pirelli tyres, wheel wake deflectors
CURRENT_GROUND_EFFECT.key_characteristics: Strict $135M financial budget cap, aerodynamic testing restriction (ATR) handicap, wake-reduction rules for close racing, extreme grid compression.

current_game_transformation_pillars.historical_state: Over-body wings and aggressive bargeboards created massive turbulent 'dirty air' wake. Following car lost 35% downforce at 20m and 46% at 10m, making close following almost impossible without tyre destruction.
current_game_transformation_pillars.current_game_state: Full Venturi underbody tunnels generate the majority of downforce via ground effect. Turbulent upwash throws dirty air over following cars; trailing car loses only 18% downforce at 10m, enabling wheel-to-wheel battles across multiple laps.
current_game_transformation_pillars.telemetry_implication: Micro-sector pace delta anomalies during close racing are now strategic tyre conservation choices rather than unavoidable wake turbulence dropouts.

current_game_transformation_pillars.historical_state: Naturally aspirated V10/V8 engines (1989-2013) had thermal efficiencies between 28% and 34%, burning 160+ kg of fuel with high mechanical failure rates (36% to 47%).
current_game_transformation_pillars.current_game_state: 1.6L Turbo V6 Power Unit paired with 120 kW MGU-K and MGU-H achieves > 52% thermal efficiency—the most efficient internal combustion engine on Earth—limited to 110 kg of fuel for an entire race.
current_game_transformation_pillars.telemetry_implication: Engine temperature anomalies are tightly constrained. A 3°C breach in ICE coolant triggers immediate MGU-K de-rate orders because drivers are strictly limited to 3-4 engines per 24-race season.

current_game_transformation_pillars.historical_state: Cars weighed ~450 kg in the 1960s and 605 kg in the V10 era, riding on 13-inch high-sidewall tyres where the tyre sidewall provided most of the mechanical suspension cushioning.
current_game_transformation_pillars.current_game_state: Current minimum weight is 798 kg (350+ kg heavier than early eras) due to the titanium Halo, reinforced carbon crash structures, and 100 kg hybrid battery pack. Riding on 18-inch low-profile Pirelli tyres.
current_game_transformation_pillars.telemetry_implication: Heavier vehicle mass amplifies lateral tyre carcass thermal degradation. Tyre temperature telemetry spikes (TEL-TYR-04) signal catastrophic blistering significantly earlier.

current_game_transformation_pillars.pillar: 4. Mechanical Reliability: From 50% Attrition to Aerospace Reliability
current_game_transformation_pillars.historical_state: In 1977-1988, 47.5% of cars retired with mechanical failures (blown turbos, cracked blocks, failed gearboxes). In 1950-1965, 44.7% suffered mechanical DNFs.
current_game_transformation_pillars.current_game_state: Mechanical DNF rate in the current 2022-2026 era has plummeted to 8.9%! Unscheduled retirements are overwhelmingly driver crashes or power unit component timeouts.
current_game_transformation_pillars.telemetry_implication: An anomaly is no longer expected operating noise. Modern telemetry anomaly detection must flag microscopic sensor deviations (0.1% thresholds) before catastrophic failure occurs.

current_game_transformation_pillars.pillar: 5. Pit Stop Speed: Sub-2-Second High-Precision Choreography
current_game_transformation_pillars.historical_state: 1950s pit stops took 40–80 seconds with manual copper wheel knock-off mallets. 1994–2009 refueling pit stops took 8.0–12.0 seconds.
current_game_transformation_pillars.current_game_state: Wheel-only stops are completed in 1.80 to 2.80 seconds stationary. Pit lane transit time is rigidly deterministic (~23.5s total).
current_game_transformation_pillars.telemetry_implication: A pit stop variance of +1.5 seconds is now a tactical anomaly that costs 3-4 positions during pit-stop undercuts.

current_game_transformation_pillars.historical_state: Top teams outspent backmarkers $450M vs $80M. Pole position was frequently 5 to 15 seconds faster than P10 in qualifying.
current_game_transformation_pillars.current_game_state: Strict $135M cost cap and sliding-scale Aerodynamic Testing Restrictions (ATR handicap where championship leader gets less wind tunnel time). In Q3, the entire top 10 is separated by < 0.4 seconds.
current_game_transformation_pillars.telemetry_implication: Milliseconds matter. A telemetry detection delay of 30 seconds allows the pit wall to switch engine mappings before a 0.2s/lap degradation costs a podium.
